No, as framed it is inadmissible. The defendant may prove his honesty only through reputation or opinion testimony (FRE 404(a)(2)(A), 405(a)), and specific instances like refusing black-marketeering offers cannot be used to prove character on direct examination. The team note's rule that past conduct must be tied to the charged transaction is not the governing standard; the bar here is the specific-instance limit on character proof. The supply-sergeant detail is at most foundation for a reputation witness, not admissible character evidence by itself.

CONFIDENCE: 80
